doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: A woman arranging with no training; Mancini's book
summary: She was the only woman writing and arranging; she learned from Henry Mancini's book and from string players.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Wow. What a story. Were you one of the few women in that level of the business at the time?

I was really the only one that did not only writing but also doing the arranging. And I hadn’t taken arranging lesson one. I got — I mean first of all I had done a lot of record dates so I had heard a lot. But — and I got some tips from good arrangers. But the, you know what’s his name the big arranger/composer, uh oh, the thing is, who is the “Moon River”—

Henry Mancini’s book, which really took the complete mystery out of it because I couldn’t imagine how those sounds were made but his book had the piano part and then a CD that had the “now you put it with these strings” “now you put it with four horns and here’s how it sounds.” Ah. And so, and of course I had the best players in the world. I

mean when I wrote, the first time I wrote a string chart — the first time I wrote a string chart the string players went [scats]. They said, “Anne, you have to put the slur over.” So that’s how much I knew. But I could, you know, get the ranges of all the instruments and one of the arrangers said, “Just don’t do anything to show off how difficult you can write.”
